subject.title: Feature request: first-class Telegram reaction triggers for agent wake-up and execution

question: Should OpenClaw resolve this issue through the shared notificationWake.reactions policy, a Telegram-specific reactionSemantics mapping, or a narrower per-message/action reaction design?
rationale: The remaining work adds public wake/config semantics and operator-control behavior, and the open candidates implement competing API shapes that automation should not choose without maintainer intent.

options.title: Repair Shared Notification Wake
options.body: Use the queue/wake/off policy from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/83611 as the default-safe canonical contract, then require rebase cleanup, precedence tests, and live Telegram proof before merge.

options.title: Adopt Telegram Semantics Mapping
options.body: Use a Telegram-specific reactionSemantics shape if maintainers want per-emoji action meanings before or instead of a cross-channel policy.

options.title: Defer Reaction Execution
options.body: Keep reactions passive for now and pause or close the implementation candidates until the product surface is clearer.

recommendation.title: Repair Shared Notification Wake
recommendation.body: Use the queue/wake/off policy from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/83611 as the default-safe canonical contract, then require rebase cleanup, precedence tests, and live Telegram proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: This person owns the open shared-policy candidate and has recent history in the reaction, config, and Telegram handler paths.
